# What an Ultrastable system is

<!-- Generated by scripts/system.py --write from autonomy/system.json and the code of record. Do not edit by hand. -->

> Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.

This is the definition every agent and every system built from this kit starts from. It is generated by `python3 scripts/system.py --write`
from `autonomy/system.json` and the code of record, and `python3 scripts/system.py --check` fails when it drifts from the code, when a clause's
probe fails in this kit, or when a standing rule has no enforcement here that is not on the declared list. Do not edit it by hand.
The prose definition is `doctrine/SYSTEM.md` (COLDSTART-1; its contract is the platform's `doctrine/coldstart.json`); this file is
the index of the code that makes them true, clause by clause, step by step and rule by rule.

## What an Ultrastable system is

- **ID-1.** An Ultrastable system is an organization of virtual managers and staff that runs itself on a server-side clock and closes its own loops. A person writes one file, IDEA.md; everything after that is the system's work. (probe: `file:IDEA.md`, `grep:bootstrap/bootstrap.py::def read\(`)
- **ID-2.** It is for something that has to keep running. An idea qualifies only when all four hold: a loop it must close, a measure that can be wrong, upkeep and improvement that never end, and a running cost the owner accepts. The bootstrapper refuses anything else before it hires a role or provisions anything. (probe: `grep:bootstrap/bootstrap.py::def qualify\(`, `grep:IDEA.md::# System test`, `grep:doctrine/VISION.md::The system test`)
- **ID-3.** Autonomous means the system has self-referential loops and the ability to close them. Every loop has a trigger, an owner, a closing probe and a write-back, and every open item has an owner, a trigger and a probe. (probe: `grep:worker/src/tick.js::async reconcile\(`, `grep:worker/src/pulse.js::export async function watch`)
- **ID-4.** The owner supplies direction, the idea and a budget. The system does the back end: errors, credentials, deploys, retries and repairs, recorded where the owner can audit them and never handed to the owner to act on. (probe: `grep:worker/src/errors.js::export function userError`, `grep:autonomy/policy.json::interrupt`)
- **ID-5.** Everything runs server-side: a Cloudflare Worker with its own D1 database and cron, and GitHub Actions on its built-in token. Nothing depends on a person's computer, a desktop app or an open chat session. (probe: `grep:worker/wrangler.template.jsonc::crons`, `grep:worker/src/index.js::async scheduled\(`)
- **ID-6.** If it is not in code, it does not exist. The repository and the database are the only memory; chat, tool memory and documents nothing reads are not storage. (probe: `grep:docs/PROJECT-MEMORY.template.md::.`, `grep:agents/AGENTS.md::If it is not in code, it does not exist`)

## How it runs

- **RUN-1.** The heartbeat is one tick every 10 minutes from the Worker's cron. A second producer, POST /pulse/watch, runs a tick when the newest one is older than two intervals, so one silent trigger never stops the clock. (probe: `grep:worker/src/index.js::async scheduled\(`, `grep:worker/src/index.js::/pulse/watch`)
- **RUN-2.** A tick runs every step listed below, and the same cron runs the loops listed after them. A failing step is recorded and filed as work, and the other steps still run. Each tick writes its report to tick_runs and /health. (probe: `grep:worker/src/tick.js::export const STEPS`, `grep:worker/src/index.js::/health`)
- **RUN-3.** Work is items with a claim, a prediction logged before the change and a closing probe after it. An item leaves the active set only with a disposition; reconcile reopens any that left without one. (probe: `grep:worker/src/tick.js::silent_drop`)
- **RUN-4.** The only pause is the interrupt gate: a step that is irreversible and identity-bound with no reversible path. It becomes one gate card with a default in effect and a closing probe; the system works on in the meantime. (probe: `grep:autonomy/policy.json::interrupt`)
- **RUN-5.** One halt stops every recurring path: the Worker variable HALT=1 stops the cron, the watch route and the webhooks. Pages keep serving. (probe: `grep:worker/src/budget.js::export function halted`)
- **RUN-6.** Every model call is paid from the owner's monthly budget through one governor; the budget is a number in the repository, never a promise. (probe: `grep:worker/src/budget.js::governedAI`)

Tick steps, in order (from `worker/src/tick.js`):

1. `migrate`: MIGRATE-SELF-1: apply pending D1 migrations through the tick's own binding (no credential), ledgered in _migrations.
2. `reconcile`: Every item that left the active set has a disposition; items whose trigger is done become ready.
3. `reap_claims`: Claims with no heartbeat for claim_ttl_minutes are released so work never stalls.
4. `connector_health`: CONNECTOR-HEALTH-1: every linked connector is read each tick (no new cron): last_ok, expires_at and the result of the refresh attempt refreshDue made just before this tick. A connector whose last two refresh attempts both failed raises one 
5. `probe_gates`: Gate cards close themselves when their probe shows the owner's step is done.
6. `score_predictions`: Predictions due now are graded against built-in metrics.
7. `measure`: OBJECTIVES-1: read every metric through its probe. Outside its healthy condition it files its own remedy item (owner, done check, closing probe) and closes that item when the probe passes again. A new system gets grace_hours before liveness
8. `accrue_trust`: Trust per (surface, action_class) from recorded outcomes; a crossed threshold opens a ladder PR item.
9. `selfaudit`: SELFAUDIT-1: probe the failure-mode register; red files or reopens FM-<id>, green closes it with evidence.
10. `unknowns`
11. `goals`: UNKNOWNS-1: question what the system does not know; the questions are plus items. GOALS-1: read every goal, sample it, move at most one knob per goal toward its target, review earlier moves, propose stretch goals, retire stale ones.
12. `plan`: PLAN-1: turn the goal furthest out of bounds into a task tree (audit > implement > verify > fix > integrate > gate), advance live plans, turn knobs itself, and gate each plan on a fresh reading of its goal. "Better" means a measured goal mo
13. `dispatch`: Roles whose tick is due pull the top ready item for their role and get a dispatch row.
14. `execute`: DOER-1: every claimed item ends done, parked with a reason, or waiting with its claim kept; nothing is left for the reaper to release unworked.
15. `check_plus_share`: Plus share over the last 20 closed items; below target opens a rebalance item for the portfolio manager.
16. `age_sla`: Q-PARITY-4 (SLA-120M): an item open past 120 minutes is raised to the top, and the cause is filed once a day; nothing ages silently. One indexed COUNT-first read (status, created_at); the per-item work only runs when the count is above zero
17. `cost_probe`: Q-COST-PROOF-2 (cost-probe): once a day, only while the free tier is ok, turn each breached cost sample into a queue item. It adds one indexed read per budget and nothing when the account is degraded (FREE_TIER_WIDE_STEPS), so it can never 
18. `pulse`: LOOPPROOF-1: every loop's expected slots against the slots it ran in; a loop that did not run files MISSED-<loop>.
19. `criticality`: CRITICALITY-1: k_eff over the rolling window; a tick may not end idle or under k_min without originating the highest-value item at the head.
20. `ignition`: BOOT-KNOWS-1: the stage from bootstrap to criticality, read from the system's own tables; the first unmet stage is IGNITE-<stage>.

Loops the same cron runs beside the tick (from `worker/src/index.js`):

- `kill-drill`: KILL-SWITCH-1: once a day the global switch is turned on, checked, turned off in every case and the test recorded
- `credentials`: AUTH-1: refresh runs first so nothing lapses
- `live-changes`: LIVE-FRESH-2: own early step; inside the sweeper it ran after 32 of 46 subrequests were spent and never wrote, so /live froze
- `fleet-changes`: PROGRESS-1: the other repositories, at most hourly each
- `substance`: SUBSTANCE-1: two merged PRs per pass are classified from their diff, so trivial merges never count as progress
- `stickiness`: STICKY-1: freshness, breadth, depth and diversity of every system's content; a stale or thin one files STICKY-<system>, and its unpromoted entries become the social queue
- `knowledge-graph`: DATAGRAPH-1: every table of this system's own D1 becomes a graph (rows are nodes, references and mentioned ids are edges), kept bi-temporally; hubs, communities, bridges and orphans are read each pass
- `graph-ai`: KGRAPH-AI-1: embeddings, extracted relations and community summaries on new graph nodes, scaled by the spend throttle
- `progress`: PROGRESS-1: release cadence monitor; a slow system has its producers dispatched, a stalled one files STALL-<system>
- `freshness`: LIVE-FRESH-2: a stale published snapshot re-dispatches its own publisher
- `gh-only`: GH-ONLY-WATCH-1: GitHub-only loops get a second clock and go live the hour Pages turns on
- `tenant-deploy`: TENANT-DEPLOY-1: a tenant repository's merge ships within the hour (twice an hour, ~4 subrequests)
- `tenant-pulse`: every tenant back end has a second route to run besides its own cron
- `repo-visibility`: declared visibility wins over drift
- `cost-samples`: D1-SNAPSHOT-1: the daily copy of D1 into the AUDIT bucket, read back before it counts

## How it bootstraps

- **BOOT-1.** bootstrap/bootstrap.py runs the stages below in order. It is idempotent: running it again changes nothing that is already true. (probe: `grep:bootstrap/bootstrap.py::for name in \("read", "constitute", "qualify"`)
- **BOOT-2.** A stage that cannot finish is recorded as blocked with its reason and becomes a backlog item with a closing probe; the boot continues with the next stage. A missing credential never stops the boot. (probe: `grep:bootstrap/bootstrap.py::def guard\(`)
- **BOOT-3.** The boot is accepted only when the system's own drills show at least a year unattended (year_gate) and its /health answers live (verify_live). (probe: `grep:bootstrap/bootstrap.py::def year_gate\(`, `grep:bootstrap/bootstrap.py::def verify_live\(`)
- **BOOT-4.** From its first deploy every system serves all of its public surfaces together: a web page with the Built on Ultrastable footer, /health, the discovery manifest, the knowledge graph's read side, and a listing in the ultrastable.io directory. No gate may hide one of them. (probe: `grep:worker/src/visibility.js::PUBLIC_READS`, `grep:worker/src/discover.js::export function manifest`, `grep:worker/src/datagraph.js::export async function readGraph`)
- **BOOT-5.** A system needs no key from its owner when it is hosted: the platform deploys it through its own OIDC route and gives it its repository from the seed. (probe: `grep:IDEA.md::hosted_by|owner_contact`, `grep:worker/src/apprepos.js::.`)

Boot stages, in order (from `bootstrap/bootstrap.py`):

1. `read`
2. `constitute`: CONSTITUTION-1: the system reads what it is before it decides anything. The constitution (doctrine/constitution.json) is checked against the code it describes and assembled into org/constitution.json (rungs, tick steps, detectors, criticali
3. `qualify`: doctrine/VISION.md: Ultrastable is for systems. Fail closed, before any role is hired or anything is provisioned.
4. `instrument`: OBJECTIVES-1: objectives and metrics are the setup that differs for every system; the liveness set is the same for all. The metric the owner declared in IDEA.md '# System test' is recorded as 'declared': a breach until a probe exists for it
5. `detect`
6. `select`
7. `cases`: Match the starting conditions against the case library: routes around each blocker, at most one owner card per blocker.
8. `plan`
9. `write`
10. `surfaces`: Health-check every route before relying on it (BG-9, BG-12). Recorded, never fatal.
11. `org`: Org initialization plan (BG-1 to BG-7, BG-11). Applied only with an admin token.
12. `provision`
13. `start`
14. `year_gate`: SEED-LAUNCH-1: the year-unattended gate is a required acceptance check for every seed. The seed's own drills run against its real recovery code (scripts/yearsim.py, autonomy/yearsim.json); the boot is accepted only when the simulated horizo
15. `verify_live`: SEED-LAUNCH-1: a boot is done only when the deployed Worker answers /health live with 200. /health answers 503 until the first complete tick, so the probe waits through one full cron interval (tick_cron, every 10 minutes) plus propagation: 

## How it becomes autonomous and reaches criticality

- **AUT-1.** The system reads its own stage every tick from evidence it recorded itself; nothing is declared. A stage is reached when the reading holds for it and every stage below, and lost when it stops holding. The first unmet stage is filed as IGNITE-<stage> with the numbers that block it, and only the same reading closes it. (probe: `grep:worker/src/ignition.js::export function judge`, `grep:worker/src/ignition.js::IGNITE-`)
- **AUT-2.** Bootstrapped means instrumented or above: the system stands, runs and measures itself. Critical and self-sustaining are the two stages above that. (probe: `grep:worker/src/ignition.js::BOOTSTRAPPED_AT = 'instrumented'`)
- **AUT-3.** Criticality is a number. k_eff = (credited verified deploys + credited loop-originated items) / (spend units + human touches) over the window. The system is critical when k_eff stays at or above k_min, and self-sustaining when it stays critical with no open ignition gaps and no human touches. (probe: `file:autonomy/criticality.json`, `grep:worker/src/criticality.js::k_eff`)
- **AUT-4.** Self-reference is the multiplier: k_self counts only deploys the system originated and shipped on itself. A deploy an outside session drove raises k_eff, never k_self. (probe: `grep:autonomy/criticality.json::"self"`)
- **AUT-5.** The standing goal is a year unattended: a simulated 10th-percentile horizon of at least 365 days, with every fault class it names drilled against the real recovery code. (probe: `grep:autonomy/goals.json::core.year.unattended`, `file:autonomy/yearsim.json`, `file:scripts/yearsim.py`)
- **AUT-6.** Trust is computed per surface and action class from recorded outcomes, and widens scope only through a reviewed change to autonomy/policy.json. Trust never reaches the interrupt gate, secrets or harness permissions. (probe: `grep:worker/src/tick.js::accrue_trust`)

The ladder from bootstrap to criticality (from `worker/src/ignition.js`; every stage is computed, never declared):

0. `unseeded`: the starting point: nothing recorded yet
1. `seeded`: the schema this code needs exists and at least one role can take work
2. `ticking`: the heartbeat completed every step for min_streak ticks in a row and missed no slot in the last hour
3. `looping`: every loop is ticking and good-slot coverage over 24 h is at least min_coverage (LOOPPROOF-1), watched by a second producer
4. `closing`: the system closed items with independently verified outcomes in the window, with no silent drop
5. `instrumented`: every objective has a probe-backed target and no metric is only declared
6. `critical`: k_eff has been at or above k_min for min_streak ticks in a row
7. `self-sustaining`: critical for sustained_ticks, with 0 open ignition gaps and 0 human touches

Criticality numbers (from `autonomy/criticality.json`): window 14 days, k_min 1, self-shipped origins executor, self-agent.

## Standing rules

98 standing rules from `agents/AGENTS.md`, each with the enforcement it cites. "In this kit" names code this repository runs;
a rule enforced only by the platform is marked so, and the platform checks it for every system it hosts.

- **USER-BACKEND-1**: The user does the idea; the system does the backend; one fix improves every system. In this kit: `doctrine/user-backend.json`, `worker/src/errors.js`, `worker/test/errors.test.js`.
- **ADMIT-1**: One tenant row admits a tenant; every registry is derived. In this kit: `worker/test/repo-settings-skip.test.js`.
- **CLAIMS-1**: Words match code. In this kit: `doctrine/claims.json`, `scripts/claims.py`.
- **VISION-1**: Vision: systems, not one-off apps. In this kit: `bootstrap/bootstrap.py`, `doctrine/VISION.md`.
- **DRAIN-ZERO-1**: Drain to zero, fleetwide. In this kit: `scripts/resolve_generated.py`.
- **INTERVIEW-1**: Interview-first, voice-first, pill-shaped input. In this kit: checked by the platform.
- **SESSION-CLOSE-1**: No zombie branches or PRs; every loop gets better. In this kit: `worker/src/sweeper.js`.
- **COMPLETE-1**: Complete everything; close everything. In this kit: `worker/src/sweeper.js`.
- **AUTO-SHIP-CLEAN-1**: Merge and deploy everything automatically; clean up everywhere. In this kit: `worker/src/handoff.js`, `worker/src/sweeper.js`.
- **DRAIN-ALL-1**: Complete all work; drain every issue; merge every PR; zero manual intervention. In this kit: `worker/src/lane.js`, `worker/src/sweeper.js`.
- **STRANGE-LOOP-1**: Strange loops: every loop closes itself and improves itself; no zombie sessions. In this kit: checked by the platform.
- **CLOCKWORK-1**: Clockwork: every loop is a clock, and a stopped or inaccurate clock is not a working clock. In this kit: `worker/src/pulse.js`.
- **FLOW-DIRECTIVE-1**: Every loop declares its flows and closes its feedback. In this kit: checked by the platform.
- **GROWTH-1**: Growth: the product manager's job is growth, not only bug fixes. In this kit: `scripts/improve.py`.
- **INSIGHT-1**: Analytics are a feedback loop, built on Cloudflare, never on an opt-in tag. In this kit: `analytics`.
- **TEMPORAL-1**: Time and iteration are part of the system; a snapshot hides what a series shows. In this kit: `scripts/trajectory.py`.
- **CONSOLE-AGENT-1**: The owner console is an agent, not a command parser. In this kit: checked by the platform.
- **SCOUT-1**: Scout the state of the art; keep improving. In this kit: `scripts/improve.py`.
- **RND-1**: R&D and competitive analysis are the product manager's job, as code. In this kit: `scripts/improve.py`.
- **AUTO-IMPROVE-1**: Autonomous audit, remediation and improvement; Quniverse parity. In this kit: checked by the platform.
- **FAILURE-RESOLVE-1**: Every failure mode is audited and every finding is taken by the queue. In this kit: `autonomy/failure-modes.json`, `worker/src/selfaudit.js`.
- **CRITICALITY-1**: Mantra, as code. In this kit: `autonomy/criticality.json`, `worker/src/criticality.js`.
- **SELF-REFERENCE-1**: Self-reference is the multiplier. In this kit: `autonomy/criticality.json`.
- **IGNORANCE-1**: The system knows what the user does not know. In this kit: checked by the platform.
- **SERVER-OWNS-LOOPS-1**: Server side owns every loop; a client never closes one. In this kit: `worker/src/sweeper.js`.
- **CODE-AGENT-SOP-1**: Code agents produce; Ultrastable owns. In this kit: `worker/src/handoff.js`, `worker/test/handoff.test.js`.
- **POINT-AND-CLICK-1**: Point and click, always; never ask a person to handle a credential. In this kit: `worker/src/auth/`.
- **CONNECT-LINK-1**: Every action only the owner can take is one link. In this kit: `worker/test/social-connect.test.js`.
- **META-SIGNAL-1**: Meta content is a signal; the microphone is monitored. In this kit: checked by the platform.
- **DESIGN-LANGUAGE-1**: One design language, many products; design is enforced and experimented, never left to chance. In this kit: `agents/roles/design-manager.md`.
- **HALT-1**: One halt stops everything; nothing is exempt. In this kit: `worker/src/budget.js`, `worker/test/budget.test.js`.
- **PROVENANCE-1**: Provenance is first-class: every input and change records where it came from and what it did. In this kit: checked by the platform.
- **WORDS-MATCH-CODE-1**: Words match code; code checks it. In this kit: `doctrine/claims.json`, `scripts/claims.py`.
- **UIUX-1**: The UI/UX manager is a closed loop: the front end does not drift into a mishmash. In this kit: `agents/roles/uiux-manager.md`.

- **CLOSED-LOOP-1**: Closed loops only; nobody reads, reviews or decides. In this kit: `autonomy/policy.json`.
- **NO-FABRICATION-1**: No made-up numbers. In this kit: `doctrine/claims.json`, `scripts/claims.py`.
- **SPEC-GATE-1**: Work items an agent cannot misread; done means proven live. In this kit: `scripts/specgate.py`.
- **STANDARDS-1**: Apply open standards; do not reinvent formats. In this kit: `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, `standards/standards.json`.
- **OUTREACH-INTRO-1**: Introduce the work; do not wait to be found. In this kit: `.github/workflows/outreach.yml`, `outreach/gate.json`, `outreach/intro-profile.json`, `outreach/prospects.json`.
- **PROMOTE-1**: Strategy and promotion are the system's job. In this kit: `worker/src/promoqueue.js`.
- **TENANT-PROMO-1**: Promotion is part of every app's and tenant's role. In this kit: `worker/src/promoqueue.js`, `worker/src/social.js`, `worker/test/promoqueue.test.js`.
- **BLINDSPOT-1**: The system knows what the owner does not. In this kit: checked by the platform.
- **UNKNOWNS-1**: Question what the system does not know; the solution space must keep growing. In this kit: `worker/src/unknowns.js`, `worker/test/unknowns.test.js`.
- **INFO-USEFUL-1**: All information is useful somehow; ingest it, keep the record in files, audit the surfaces. In this kit: checked by the platform.
- **SUBSTANCE-1**: Only behaviour counts; no illusion of productivity. In this kit: `worker/src/vendor/core/substance.js`.
- **PROGRESS-1**: Visible progress at every visit, for six months with no input. In this kit: `worker/src/progress.js`, `worker/test/progress.test.js`.
- **RUNWAY-1**: A year unattended, measured. In this kit: `scripts/seedlife.py`, `scripts/yearsim.py`.
- **DISPOSE-1**: Nothing sits in the queue; every item gets a coded disposition. In this kit: `worker/src/sla.js`, `worker/src/tick.js`.
- **NO-OPEN-ITEMS-1**: No open items, ever. In this kit: `worker/src/tick.js`.
- **SEED-LIFECYCLE-1**: A seed is not done until it runs a year unattended. In this kit: `autonomy/seed-lifecycle.json`, `scripts/seedlife.py`.
- **SEED-AUTONOMY-1**: A seed that answers is not yet a seed that runs itself. In this kit: `bootstrap/bootstrap.py`, `scripts/seedadmit.py`, `tests/test_seed.py`, `worker/src/index.js`.
- **TEMPLATE-CODE-ONLY-1**: The template is code only. In this kit: checked by the platform.
